facts: Battery recycling reduces the number of batteries disposed as municipal solid waste.
Batteries contain heavy metals and toxic chemicals.
Disposing of batteries by the same process as regular household waste raises concerns over soil contamination and water pollution.
The Battery Directive of the European Union requires increased recycling of batteries.
The Battery Directive of the European Union promotes research on improved battery recycling methods.
All batteries sold within the EU must be marked with the collection symbol, which is a crossed-out wheeled bin.
The Rechargeable Battery Recycling Corporation operates a battery recycling program called Call2Recycle in the United States and Canada.
Most jurisdictions regulate battery handling and disposal to reduce mercury discharge.
Silver oxide batteries can be recycled to recover mercury.
In 2005, the rechargeable battery collection rate was 5.6%.
Alkaline batteries must not be thrown in with domestic waste in Europe.
Businesses that sell new car batteries may collect used batteries for recycling.
Battery recycling of automotive batteries reduces the need for resources for new battery manufacture.
Battery recycling of automotive batteries diverts toxic lead from landfills.
Battery recycling of automotive batteries prevents the risk of improper disposal.
A used lead-acid battery is classified as hazardous waste under the Basel Convention.
Batteries are a form of electronic waste.
E-waste recycling services recover toxic substances for use in new batteries.
